title: RSE 6/12: Solar eclipse local circumstances (eclipse_how)
description:
### Summary
Port `eclipse_how` (local circumstances at an observer: magnitude, obscuration, contact geometry, az/alt) and its public wrapper `swe_sol_eclipse_how`. Exposes `Ephemeris::sol_eclipse_how` (`&self`).

Depends on **RSE 5** (eclipse module, `calc_planet_star`, constants) and **RSE 2** (`swe_azalt`) and **RSE 1** (topocentric `calc` — this uses `TOPOCTR|EQUATORIAL` Sun/Moon positions).

### Files
- `src/eclipse.rs` — add `EclipseHow` (attr) result struct, `eclipse_how`, `swe_sol_eclipse_how`.
- `src/context.rs` — `pub fn sol_eclipse_how(&self, tjd_ut, ifl: CalcFlags, geopos:[f64;3]) -> Result<EclipseHow, Error>`.
- `src/lib.rs` — re-export `EclipseHow`.
- `tests/c-gen/gen_eclipse.c` — add key `sol_how`; regenerate `eclipse.json`.
- `tests/golden/eclipse.rs` — add `#[test] sol_how`.

### Implementation steps
Read `docs/c-ref-eclipse-solar.md` §4.1–§4.11.

1. **`EclipseHow`** result: name fields per the `attr[]` index table in §4.9 (`attr[0]`=magnitude, `attr[1]`=diameter ratio, `attr[2]`=obscuration, `attr[3]`=core shadow, `attr[4]`=azimuth, `attr[5]`=true altitude, `attr[6]`=apparent altitude, `attr[7]`=elongation, `attr[8]`=NASA magnitude, `attr[9]`=... — copy exactly from §4.9).
2. **`eclipse_how`** (§4): setup (§4.1) — topocentric `calc(... TOPOCTR|EQUATORIAL)` for Sun & Moon via `self.calc` with `config.topographic` set from `geopos`; az/alt via `swe_azalt` (§4.2); angular radii + centre separation (§4.3); phase classification (§4.4); magnitude `attr[0]` = `(-dctr + rsun + rmoon)/(2*rsun)`, ratio `attr[1]` (§4.5); obscuration `attr[2]` via the circular-segment lens-area formula (§4.6 — spelled out; preserve the exact segment algebra); visibility threshold (§4.7); NASA magnitude + Saros (§4.8).
   - **STATELESS NOTE:** C calls `swe_set_topo` then reads `swed.topd`. Here, build a per-call `Ephemeris` view whose `config.topographic = Some(TopoPosition::from(geopos))`, OR pass `geopos` into an internal topocentric-calc helper. Do NOT mutate `self`. If threading topo through `calc` is awkward, add a private `calc_topo(&self, geopos, jd, body, flags)` that clones config with the observer set (same pattern as `houses_ex2`'s `deltat_config` clone at context.rs:286).
3. **`swe_sol_eclipse_how`** (§4.11): public wrapper; note (§4.11) its horizon-visibility override can zero the whole result when the eclipse is below the horizon — replicate.

### C reference
`docs/c-ref-eclipse-solar.md` §4 (all subsections), §0 (radii constants).

### Golden tests
- **C harness** add key `sol_how`: for the same eclipse epochs as `sol_where` and observers `geopos ∈ {(8.55,47.37,500), (-100.0,40.0,0)}` (one near-central, one off-track), call `swe_sol_eclipse_how(tjd_ut, SEFLG_MOSEPH, geopos, attr, serr)`. Emit `{tjd_ut, geopos, retval, attr:[0..11]}`. Regenerate `eclipse.json`.
- **Rust test** `#[test] sol_how`: assert `attr` fields via `assert_f64_eps(.., 1e-7)`; assert returned flags == `retval`.
- `cargo test --test golden eclipse::sol_how -- --nocapture` passes.

### Acceptance criteria
- `cargo build` + `cargo clippy --all-targets` clean.
- `cargo test --test golden eclipse::sol_how -- --nocapture` passes (1e-7).

### Escape hatch
If `attr` fails > 1e-6 after two attempts, STOP and report which `attr[]` index diverges. Read `swecl.c:967–1152` directly. Escalate to Opus after two attempts.
execution_record: Read swecl.c directly (not just the ref doc) for two things the ref doc explicitly left out as raw data: the 181-entry saros_data_solar[] table (swecl.c:107-298, transcribed verbatim into a `const [(i32, f64); 181]`) and the exact eclipse_how/swe_sol_eclipse_how bodies (swecl.c:922-1157) to confirm loop/branch structure the ref doc summarized. No other divergence from the task brief -- implemented calc_planet_star_topo (topo-config-aware variant of calc_planet_star, planet branch only, stars still unsupported for TOPOCTR matching riseset.rs's existing limitation), eclipse_how, EclipseHow, sol_eclipse_how, Ephemeris::sol_eclipse_how, gen_eclipse.c sol_how key (8 cases: 4 sol_where epochs x 2 observers), and the Rust golden test. All golden cases passed on the first run (no debugging cycle needed).

Notes (shared with 74/75 review): compiled binary tests/c-gen/gen_eclipse (992KB) was committed in 9bd1c62 and recommitted in d735aa0/f5371ca — siblings are untracked/ignored; recommend git rm --cached + gitignore.
